programme.desc: A morning rush to work results in a tussle between Dhruv and Kavya, spoiling their moods. Throughout the day, they attempt to make amends, highlighting the irony and sweetness of their relationship.

programme.title: Good Night
programme.desc: A sleepless night due to mosquitoes leads to the discovery that Kavya's ex-boyfriend is getting married, prompting a long conversation about their past relationships.

programme.title: Thank You!
programme.desc: Plans for a dinner at an Iranian restaurant get canceled, leading Dhruv and Kavya to attend a friend's house party. The night evolves into an unexpected adventure, ending at a local fair.

programme.title: Here We Go!
programme.desc: During a visit to a vineyard, Dhruv and Kavya open up about their insecurities and future aspirations, leading to deeper conversations about life and their relationship.

programme.title: Masterji
programme.desc: Kishore, an orphan has only one dream, to join the IndianArmy. When he gets thrown out of his orphanage, Masterji, an ex-army officer who left the army and is now working as a tailor, reluctantly adopts him. The khadoos Masterji and Kishore have only two things in common, their dream to serve the nation and their lonely lives. Will Masterji help Kishore achieve his own unfulfilled dreams to become a soldier, and will Kishore find a father in Masterji?

programme.title: Jaldi Lautna, Captain
programme.desc: Captain Vikrant Sahay and his wife Vibha had a beautiful love story. But Vikrant’s sudden death in battle leaves the otherwise happy-go-lucky Vibha completely shocked. Unable to deal with Vikrant’s death, Vibha decides that the best way to honor him is to fulfill his dream, by joining the army herself, much against her family’s wishes. Will Vibha succeed and make her late husband, her family, and the country proud?

programme.title: Shooter Jawan
programme.desc: Tribhuvan, a dedicated Indian Army Officer comes across a young sweeper Tinku, who is a gifted shooter. Tribhuvan knows Tinku has a rare talent, and wants to enroll him in the shooting academy and then the Indian Army. However, owing to Tinku’s caste, his father is afraid of society’s taunts and is completely against this career choice. Will Tinku have the courage to fight back and rise above ‘log kya kahenge’?

programme.title: Sarhad Ke Baad Bhi
programme.desc: Colonel Balram, a retired Indian Army Officer, returns home after several years of service, only to find himself completely disconnected from his son Aman. While Balram is failing at mending his relationship with Aman, he is also silently struggling with mental health issues, because of his days at war. Will Aman ever understand his father’s sacrifices for the country or will it be too late before he realises just how much his father loves him?

programme.title: Veera
programme.desc: Veera’s martyred father’s last wish was for her to join the Indian armed forces. But Veera is not for it. The bravery and patriotism that the country remembers and celebrates him for, are the same things that took Veera’s father away from her. She’s been carrying this anger and hurt in her heart for too long, until she discovers a hidden letter.

programme.title: Bachelorhood
programme.desc: Viraj and Arjun have been best friends since childhood. While Viraj loves his bachelor life and wants Arjun to move in as his flatmate, Arjun has other plans of ‘settling down’. What happens when this bachelor reveals he wants to be ‘unbachelored?’

programme.title: Kabab Mein Haddi
programme.desc: The gang gets together to celebrate Arjun’s big news, but Viraj is concerned whether the dynamics of the group will change with its new addition. Will Khushi win over the gang and get Viraj's stamp of approval?

programme.title: (un)happy Birthday
programme.desc: Its Arjun’s birthday, and Khushi steals the limelight with her unconventional celebration party. Tensions at the party rise when Viraj confronts Arjun about his change in behaviour since he started dating Khushi. Will Arjun pick pyaar or dosti?

programme.title: Mann Ki Rant
programme.desc: The group tries to resolve tensions between Viraj and Arjun, but they both resist. As Viraj rants to Zara and Kaka about his friendships and relationships, he realises more about his true self.

programme.title: Yaar Ki Shaadi
programme.desc: The wedding day is here! Will Viraj stand by Arjun on the most important day of his life, and will he admit his true feelings to a special someone?

programme.title: Conflict Of Interest
programme.desc: Shagun wants to keep the Filmy Weddings business floating and for that she’s willing to go to any lengths. Even if it means shooting a wedding film for Adhira’s ex-boyfriend – Akhil. Adhira is furious and tries her best to sabotage the entire project. Unfortunately, her one big hurdle is Dad, who has taken quite a fondness for Akhil. Check out the episode and find out what happens next!

programme.title: Internal Politics
programme.desc: Adhira and Shagun are in a disagreement about whom to select for a wedding film promo: a boring aunt from the bride's side or a lively drunk aunt from the groom's family. Things take a turn for the complicated when the parents also weigh in with their respective biases.

programme.title: Poaching The Talent
programme.desc: Vishnu, the Agarwal's househelp cum man friday is desired by the sisters as an office boy to help them sort out their business affairs. The parents are naturally opposed to the idea. Thus begins another standoff in the Agarwal household - and Vishnu's position in the house is at stake. Who will finally lay claim over Vishnu's priceless services?

programme.title: Business Secrets
programme.desc: In a footage from a wedding they just filmed, the sisters find a drunken confession from the bride's best friend. It turns out she is the groom's ex - and he hasn't told the bride to be. Caught in the moral dilemma of choosing to tell the bride or not, the sisters find themselves on other ends of the argument. Meanwhile, it is revealed that Adhira's father might have a similar secret hidden from everyone. Will the sisters do the morally right thing or the financially right thing? And what is the father's bizarre obsession with knowing who the groom's mom is?

programme.title: Breach Of Contract
programme.desc: Chasing a competitive business pitch to work for a coveted fashion firm, the sisters are again at different sides of a dilemma. The commitment to the new opportunity would be for a minimum two years, which Adhira is reluctant to make at the age of 25. Whereas Shagun, having already quit her high paying corporate job to join this business, sees no harm in seizing the opportunity with open arms. As their argument turns to a fight, we are left wondering if this is in fact the fight to end all fights. Will the sisters come to the same page and work for the pitch? Or will Happily Hitched disband for good?

programme.title: Arranged Family
programme.desc: Nikhil Solanki arrives at his in-laws' home, where a series of mishaps culminate in a significant blunder that upsets his father-in-law, Prakash Sharma. Both struggle to address the situation openly.

programme.title: The Mad House
programme.desc: Prakash avoids acknowledging that Nikhil damaged his car, instead blaming neighborhood children. Nikhil's attempts to rectify the situation lead to further complications.

programme.title: Conditions Apply
programme.desc: During Sudha and Prakash's anniversary celebration, relatives pose uncomfortable questions, challenging Nikhil's patience and composure.

programme.title: Stuck In The Middle
programme.desc: A disagreement between Anita and her parents results in a cold war, leaving Nikhil caught between his wife and in-laws.

programme.title: Home
programme.desc: Nikhil expresses his feelings of being an outsider within the family, prompting an open discussion aimed at resolving underlying issues.

programme.title: Welcome Home
programme.desc: A few months after moving to Mumbai, Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita are finally settled. The peace is interrupted by the arrival of Nikhil's parents, Kiran (Shishir Sharma) and Vandana (Renuka Shahane), for a short visit. Anita, ever the perfectionist, is anxious to be the "perfect daughter-in-law," but her efforts are met with a series of awkward and hilarious hurdles.

programme.title: Surprise, Surprise!
programme.desc: The episode picks up with the fallout of Nikhil’s father, Kiran (Shishir Sharma), going missing during his walk in the previous episode. While he eventually returns, the tension doesn't dissipate. The "surprise" of the title is twofold: the unexpected arrival of Nikhil’s sister, Shreya (Kriti Vij), and the unsettling realization that something is physically or mentally "off" with Kiran.

programme.title: Spilling The Beans
programme.desc: The entire family—Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh), Anita (Eisha Chopra), Kiran (Shishir Sharma), Vandana (Renuka Shahane), and Shreya (Kriti Vij)—piles into a car to attend a relative's 60th birthday celebration. What was meant to be a joyful getaway becomes a pressure cooker for the long-standing resentment between the siblings.

programme.title: Something's Missing
programme.desc: The title is a poignant double entendre: it refers to a missing set of rings at the family function, but more deeply, it refers to the "missing" pieces of Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) memory. The facade of a "normal family vacation" finally crumbles, forcing the Solankis to stop pretending.

programme.title: House Of Cards
programme.desc: The title "House of Cards" refers to the fragile "perfect family" image the Solankis have tried to maintain. After the emotional explosion regarding Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) health and Shreya’s (Kriti Vij) marriage, the "house" has finally collapsed—but in its place, something more honest is being built.

programme.title: Home
programme.desc: In the Season 2 finale, "Home," Anita and Nikhil prepare to move into their own place. The episode resolves the season's friction between Anita and her mother-in-law, replacing awkward formalities with genuine mutual respect. As they move out, the story concludes that "home" isn't about physical space, but the emotional bridge built between two different generations.

programme.title: Circle Of Life
programme.desc: The title "Circle of Life" refers to the poignant role reversal where the children now become the guardians of their parents, mirroring the care they once received.

programme.title: Not Kidding
programme.desc: The episode centers on a visit from Anita’s boisterous, unfiltered parents—Akshata (Deepika Amin) and Kiran Sharma (Shishir Sharma). The quiet, disciplined, and currently somber Solanki household is suddenly upended by the high-energy Sharmas. The primary conflict arises when the two sets of parents have a "polite clash" over how to care for the ailing Kiran Solanki and, more pivotally, the couple's future plans regarding children.

programme.title: Here We Go Again
programme.desc: With the house now fully "merged," Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) decide to throw a surprise anniversary party for the "Folks." While their intentions are pure, the episode explores how a "celebration" can quickly become a source of stress when dealing with a chronic illness and interfering relatives.

programme.title: Zor Se Bolo
programme.desc: The episode revolves around a chaotic Sunday at the Solanki household. The central plot involves Kiran Solanki (Shishir Sharma) needing a hearing aid, but it quickly spirals into a larger commentary on how the family members are "deaf" to each other's actual needs and desires.

programme.title: That's All Folks
programme.desc: The finale moves away from the day-to-day bickering and centers on a quiet realization: Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Eisha Chopra) have finally stopped "adjusting" and have started living. The episode focuses on the family accepting their "New Normal" while acknowledging that the road ahead with Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) health will be challenging but shared.

programme.title: Truth Bombs
programme.desc: The episode begins with Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Esha Chopra) gathering the family for a "serious talk." After months of private deliberation, they drop the ultimate truth bomb: they have decided to adopt a child instead of pursuing a biological pregnancy.

programme.title: The Damaad Test
programme.desc: The episode centers on the Home Study, a critical step in the Indian adoption process where a government social worker visits the family to determine if they are fit to raise a child. However, the title "The Damaad Test" (The Son-in-law Test) refers to the parallel pressure Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) feels to prove he is a "good son" while also being a "good son-in-law" to Anita’s (Eisha Chopra) visiting parents.

programme.title: Ladkiwale Vs. Ladkewale
programme.desc: While Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) are stuck in the agonizing "waiting period" of the CARA process, the tension shifts to the two sets of parents. The episode highlights that even when everyone agrees on the goal (the grandchild), their different ways of expressing love and anxiety can lead to a hilarious yet deep-seated cultural clash.

programme.title: Are We Ready?
programme.desc: The wait is over: Anita and Nikhil are matched with a child. However, instead of the pure euphoria they expected, they are hit with a wave of intense anxiety. The title "Are We Ready?" reflects the internal crisis the couple faces as they realize their lives are about to change irrevocably—not in nine months, but in a matter of days.

programme.title: What The Future?
programme.desc: The finale begins with the arrival of the moment Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) have spent the entire season preparing for: bringing their adopted daughter home. The episode isn't just about the new arrival, but about how each family member adapts to their "What The Future" role.

programme.title: Comfort Zone
programme.desc: Shaurya struggles with getting recognition for his efforts at work while Sanya debates shifting out of her home. Both of them help each other step out of their comfort zones and grow

programme.title: Time Off
programme.desc: As Shaurya and Sanya shift in together, Sanya takes a gamble at work which impacts both of their lives.

programme.title: Emotion Or Logic
programme.desc: As Shaurya and Sanya deal with the realization of having fallen for each other, they have to prioritize what is more important - emotions or logic?

programme.title: New Roles
programme.desc: Having finally admitted their feelings to each other, Shaurya and Sanya's honeymoon weekend is over and they must get back to reality. With Shaurya up for a promotion and Sanya doubtful about her growth in this company, what is this new couple in for?

programme.title: Milestones
programme.desc: With appraisals around the corner, Shaurya and Sanya brace themselves for the unexpected. Eventually, Shaurya gets his first real lesson in team management and Sanya makes a crucial decision to help her get what she wants.

programme.title: Month-Iversary
programme.desc: To mark 3 months of being together, Shaurya convinces Sanya to organise something for their "monthiversary." However, things begin to get complicated as Shaurya finds himself working directly with Sanya - for the first time since they started dating.

programme.title: Choices
programme.desc: Shaurya eventually ends up at Akhil’s party but to his surprise does not feel like he belongs there. Meanwhile, Ratna invites Sanya to have a drink with her. Sanya still upset about Shaurya lying to her begins to feel better with Ratna and her friends. To her surprise Shaurya shows up there as well to save their monthi-versary. However, things seem to go in the opposite direction soon.

programme.title: Time Off
programme.desc: Shaurya’s presentation does not go as planned and he ends up overpromising samples to the client on a three day deadline. This leads to the team having to work round the clock. Meanwhile, Sanya makes a plan to take a break from work and convinces Shaurya to do go somewhere together. Both Shaurya and Sanya finally spend some quality time with each other but things take a turn when Shaurya gets a call from Vinod.

programme.title: Last Shot
programme.desc: Sanya decides to move back to her room. Shaurya isn’t happy about this. To make things worse Akhil is hard on him for overpromising and almost losing the client. Akhil demands that the team fixes the situation and gets them another chance.

programme.title: Broke Af
programme.desc: The episode sets the stage for the series: Ray and Nikhat are best friends and roommates who have just started their journey into independent adulthood. The central conflict is the classic "End of the Month" crisis—where your bank account is empty, but your social and survival needs are not.

programme.title: Mommy Knows Best
programme.desc: The episode centers on a surprise visit from Nikhat’s mother, which triggers a high-speed cleaning operation. For any young person living away from home, the "parental visit" is a performance of maturity, and Ray and Nikhat are determined to win an Oscar for "Most Responsible Adults."

programme.title: Friends Ya Followers
programme.desc: The episode explores the gap between digital perception and reality. Ray and Nikhat find themselves caught in a cycle of comparing their "boring" lives to the filtered, high-glamour lives of their peers on Instagram.

programme.title: On My Way
programme.desc: The episode follows a high-stakes day for both girls. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) is trying to climb the corporate ladder and has a critical presentation, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is dealing with the thrill and anxiety of a potential romantic connection. The title reflects the constant "hustle" and the physical and metaphorical state of being "in transit" in life.

programme.title: Now And Then
programme.desc: The episode is framed around a significant milestone: Nikhat’s (Aisha Ahmed) birthday. While birthdays are usually for celebrating, they often trigger a "Quarter-Life Crisis" where we compare our current reality to the versions of ourselves we imagined "then."

programme.title: Just Kiddin
programme.desc: The episode revolves around the nightmare of moving houses in Mumbai. Ray and Nikhat are excited about their new "adult" space, but the transition from the old house to the new one becomes a comedy of errors that tests their patience and their friendship.

programme.title: Work It Out
programme.desc: The episode explores the "Work-Life Balance" myth. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), now in a senior role with a fancy new apartment to pay for, is buried under deadlines, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is trying to figure out how to be a "productive" freelancer without the structure of an office.

programme.title: Me Vs Us
programme.desc: The episode centers on the loss of personal space. As Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) spend more time in their new apartment, the "honeymoon phase" of moving in ends. The title reflects the struggle to maintain one’s own identity ("Me") while being part of a co-dependent duo ("Us").

programme.title: Not Cool
programme.desc: The episode centers on the arrival of Ray’s (Yashaswini Dayama) old school friend. Ray is excited to show off her "cool" Mumbai life, her "cool" roommate Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), and her "cool" new apartment. However, the reunion doesn't go as planned, leading to a major case of "Social Comparison Anxiety."

programme.title: Challenge Accepted
programme.desc: Everything that could go wrong, does. The episode is a "comedy of errors" that quickly turns into an emotional crucible. As the girls juggle professional disasters and personal health scares, they are forced to answer the question: Are we just friends because it’s convenient, or are we family?

programme.title: Pawri Ho Rahi Hai
programme.desc: The episode picks up with Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) feeling the absolute peak of urban exhaustion. Between Nikhat’s soul-crushing corporate deadlines and Ray’s chaotic freelance schedule, they realize they are running on fumes. To blow off some steam before their planned trip home, they decide to have one last "epic" Mumbai night.

programme.title: Rat Trap
programme.desc: The episode follows Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) as they settle into their respective family homes. The initial "pampering phase" (where parents cook your favorite meals and do your laundry) ends abruptly, replaced by the suffocating routine and expectations they once ran away from.

programme.title: Old Dots, New Lines
programme.desc: While still in their respective hometowns, Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) encounter people from their past. The episode highlights the awkward friction that occurs when you realize your old friends have either stayed exactly the same or changed in ways you can no longer relate to.

programme.title: Sisterhood
programme.desc: The episode explores the complex, multi-generational layers of female relationships. It’s not just about the friendship between the two leads, but about the "sisterhood" they share with their mothers and the realization that their mothers were once young, ambitious, and confused women too.

programme.desc: The video shows how an arranged marriage scenario would look if everyone were completely honest. It highlights awkward truths, funny realities, and relatable family pressure.

programme.title: When You're Single But Your Best Friend Isn't
programme.desc: The video humorously shows the struggles of being single when your best friend is dating. It highlights the awkward, funny moments and feelings of being left out.

programme.title: When You Are The Youngest In The Group
programme.desc: You’re the baby everyone teases, lectures, and secretly protects—a mix of irritation and affection rolled into one.

programme.title: Why Girl Best Friends Are So Special
programme.desc: The video shows the funny and heartfelt moments that make having a girl best friend so special. From sharing secrets to standing by each other in every situation, it celebrates the bond of true friendship.

programme.title: Absent Minded Things We All Do (part 2)
programme.desc: Highlights common, everyday absent-minded habits that many people can relate to—such as forgetting why you walked into a room or misplacing items. It’s the second part in a series dedicated to showcasing these quirky, relatable moments.

programme.title: Signs Romance Has No Age Limit
programme.desc: The video shows how love and romance remain special at any age. It highlights the sweet, funny, and heartwarming moments that prove romance knows no boundaries of time.

programme.title: If Teachers Could Hear Your Thoughts
programme.desc: A humorous take on what would happen if teachers could actually hear the unfiltered thoughts of their students — revealing all the sarcasm, boredom, and chaos that usually stay inside their heads.

programme.title: If You Could Hear Your Colleague's Thoughts
programme.desc: What your co-workers really think: the yawns, the “why did they email me this?”, the lunchtime strategies. The video explores the humorous disconnect between office faces and internal thoughts.

programme.title: Savage Mom Vs Savage Daughter
programme.desc: Two strong personalities — mother and daughter — going head to head in witty comebacks, power games, and hidden affection. It shows how love and defiance intertwine in that bond.

programme.title: 5 Tough Decisions Teenagers Have To Make
programme.desc: This FilterCopy video explores the tricky and relatable choices teenagers face growing up. Alam Khan and Devishi Madaan bring to life five common but tough decisions that test a teen’s judgment, emotions, and priorities.

programme.title: What Moms Say Vs What They Mean
programme.desc: Everyday conversations with Mom are shown with the “surface” meaning and the hidden real meaning—because what she says (“Do what you want”) is often not what she means (“Don’t you dare!”)

programme.title: When Your Partner Gets Mad At You
programme.desc: A funny look at how people react when their partner gets mad — from desperate attempts to apologize to over-the-top efforts to make things right, capturing the relatable drama of every relationship fight.

programme.title: Fashion Conversations With Mom
programme.desc: The video humorously portrays the generational clash in fashion choices between moms and kids. It highlights funny disagreements, quirky comments, and relatable family moments.

programme.title: Can Exes Be Friends
programme.desc: The video explores the question of whether ex-partners can truly remain friends after a breakup, showcasing everyday scenes that highlight the tension and awkwardness in such dynamics.

programme.title: Things Science Students Are Tired Of Hearing
programme.desc: The video shows the repetitive and annoying questions science students often hear. It highlights the frustration, confusion, and funny reactions that come from constantly explaining their field to others.

programme.title: Flatmates: First Month Vs Now
programme.desc: The video humorously contrasts the first month of living with flatmates—where everything’s perfect, new, and exciting—with the “now” phase, where laziness, weird habits, and annoyances have crept in.

programme.title: When Your Partner Is Into Fitness
programme.desc: Your fitness-obsessed partner influences every meal, routine, and outing, sometimes to extremes. The video shows how your relationship adjusts — from diet talks to gym push pressures.

programme.title: When You Try To Quit Smoking
programme.desc: The internal battle, cravings, relapses, and justifications you go through attempting to quit. The video dramatizes how every trigger, slip, and “just one more” happens in your head.

programme.title: Reality Of Having Anxiety
programme.desc: This video realistically portrays the everyday struggles of living with anxiety. It highlights common experiences like overthinking conversations , feeling self-conscious in social situations, and the physical symptoms of anxiety such as sweating palms, shortness of breath, and fatigue.

programme.title: Struggles Of Exam Prep
programme.desc: The all-too-real chaos of exam season: the sleepless nights, panic Google searches, last-minute revision, family pressure and the weird peace when the exam sheet finally drops.

programme.title: When You Are A Dog Parent
programme.desc: The joys and weirdness of treating your dog like your child: the endless photos, checking if they’re okay when you’re away, the guilt, the silly little routines, the unconditional love wrapped in fur.

programme.title: Wedding Romance: Falling In Love At Your Bff's Wedding | Part 2 Ft.
programme.desc: At your best friend's wedding you unexpectedly fall for someone: the stolen glances during the ceremony, the shared laughter in a corner, and the dilemma of a new beginning in an old friendship setting.

programme.title: Every Introvert Ever
programme.desc: This video comically depicts the relatable struggles and unique behaviors of introverts. It showcases situations like avoiding social gatherings, pretending to be busy to escape conversations, and finding joy in solitude, all while highlighting the inner world of an introvert

programme.title: Things We Did In College
programme.desc: The free-spirited college days: late-night chats, spontaneous plans, weird life lectures from friends, figure-out-your-future stress, tons of memories that become “remember when” moments later.

programme.title: When Your Sibling Knows Your Secret
programme.desc: That moment when your sibling drops a bomb–they know that thing you thought was buried forever—and the mix of panic, betrayal and relief that follows.

programme.title: The Boyfriend We All Deserve
programme.desc: A girl daydreams about the perfect boyfriend who gets her jokes, supports her quirks and is weirdly in sync with her mood swings. Reality then hits when she realises the gap between “ideal-boyfriend” and the human beside her.

programme.title: When You And Your Bff Are Complete Opposites
programme.desc: The one who’s impulsive and the one who plans; one loves the party and the other loves the book; yet you find a weird balance and strength in the fact that you’re totally different.

programme.title: If Office Were Like A Jungle
programme.desc: The wild ecosystem of office life, complete with predators (bosses), scavengers (gossipers), and survivors (you).

programme.title: Almost Shaadi At 4am
programme.desc: A hilarious “shaadi scene” unfolds in the dead of night when chaos, confusion, and last-minute wedding madness collide — because in every Indian wedding, something always goes wrong.

programme.title: Introvert Or Extrovert: Which One Are You?
programme.desc: The video humorously explores the quirks of both introverts and extroverts. It highlights their contrasting personalities and how they navigate everyday life.

programme.title: First Time And Girls
programme.desc: The excitement, nerves, awkwardness and bonding between girlfriends as they talk about/wonder about doing something for the “first time”—whatever “first time” means for them in that moment.

programme.title: Every College Romance
programme.desc: The coffee chats, late-night study groups that turn into deep talks, “let’s hang out” that become more than just notes swapping—and the inevitable chaos when love and exams clash.

programme.title: Thoughts You Have During A Haircut
programme.desc: As you sit in the salon chair you’re thinking: “Just a trim… keep it more than last time… hope they don’t mess it up…” — and your mind wanders. The video captures that internal monologue everyone has during a haircu

programme.title: A Day Without Electricity
programme.desc: How modern life collapses when the power’s out—no Wi-Fi, no AC, no Netflix—just panic, sweat, and forced bonding.

programme.title: If Google Were An Indian Aunty
programme.desc: The video humorously imagines Google behaving like a nosy Indian aunty. It highlights funny situations of over-involvement, unsolicited advice, and curious questions.

programme.title: Can Genz And Millennials Be Friends?
programme.desc: This video explores whether Gen Z and Millennials can truly be friends, highlighting their distinct traits and humorous cultural clashes. It showcases their differing approaches to work, relationships, and daily life, ultimately demonstrating how they navigate their friendship despite generational gaps.

programme.title: Awkward Moments With Your Crush
programme.desc: A compilation of hilariously cringe-worthy moments when your crush is around: the flustered smiles, mis-sent messages, the sudden silence when they walk in. All the awkwardness you try so hard to hide, front and centre.

programme.title: Lockdown Wala Birthday
programme.desc: The video humorously portrays what it’s like to celebrate a birthday during lockdown. It highlights missed traditions, creative adjustments, and the joy of simple celebrations.

programme.title: Every Long Distance Relationship
programme.desc: The late-night calls, bad network, missed birthdays, emotional reunions, and the constant tug between love and distance.

programme.title: Unlucky Moments That Ruin Your Day
programme.desc: The tiny tragedies—spilling coffee, missing the bus, dropping your phone—that somehow set off an entire day of bad luck.

programme.title: Every Office Bff
programme.desc: The video humorously showcases the special bond between office best friends. It highlights their gossip, support, and fun moments that make work bearable.

programme.title: What Moms Want Vs What They Get
programme.desc: A mom dreams of rest, praise, time with her kids — but she gets missed calls, last-minute pick-ups and zero sleep. The video uses humour and heart to contrast her wish-list versus real-life.

programme.title: Reality Of A Topper
programme.desc: Being a topper may seem like the ultimate dream—achieving the highest grades, getting all the accolades, and being the ""golden child."" But what’s the reality behind the perfect grades? The pressure, the expectations, and yes, the constant battle to stay at the top. In this hilarious sketch, we take a closer look at the life of a topper and what it's really like behind the shining medals.

programme.title: If Ekta Kapoor Directed Your Life
programme.desc: The video imagines daily life as if it were directed by Ekta Kapoor. It highlights dramatic reactions, over-the-top scenarios, and hilarious soap opera twists.

programme.title: The Razor Effect
programme.desc: One small action — like shaving / grooming — triggers a cascade of changes in attitude, confidence and how others treat you. The video shows how a little upgrade (razor, haircut) leads to big perceptions.

programme.title: Struggles Of House Cleaning
programme.desc: This video comically illustrates the various difficulties and challenges faced while attempting to clean a house. It highlights the often-relatable struggles of maintaining a clean living space

programme.title: Things Sisters Do
programme.desc: A sister-sister relationship: prank calls, borrowing clothes, fighting over the mirror, then insisting “I got you, always.” The video highlights the unique mix of rivalry and love sisters share.

programme.title: When Your Bff Is Leaving School
programme.desc: The bittersweet countdown: the late chats, the “let’s do something memorable” mood, packing up memories, and the quiet fear of “will things be the same after you go?”

programme.title: If Your Wife Could Hear Your Thoughts
programme.desc: A husband’s internal monologue meets the reality of his wife apparently reading his mind—every unspoken thought becomes a comedic disaster waiting to happen.

programme.title: School Best Friends During Lockdown
programme.desc: Online classes, missed canteen gossip, and the nostalgia of school friendships during isolation.

programme.title: When Girls Fall For Red Flags
programme.desc: A witty portrayal of how girls knowingly ignore every warning sign in relationships, convincing themselves that red flags are just “misunderstood.”

programme.title: When He Doesn’t Like You Back
programme.desc: You think maybe he does, you hope he might, you plan how you’ll act—but deep down you always know: the answer might be “no”; the video shows the sting of un-reciprocated feelings and how you deal.

programme.title: When Your Sibling Comes Home After A Long Time
programme.desc: The excitement, the over-preparing, the sibling rivalry resurfacing, and the joy of rediscovering the quirks you’d missed while they were away.

programme.title: Break-Up Ke Stages
programme.desc: This video humorously explores the various emotional stages people go through after a breakup, depicting the struggles and eventual healing process. It shows the journey of moving on and attempting to cut contact, highlighting the complexities of post-breakup emotions.

programme.title: Love-Hate Relationship With Older Siblings
programme.desc: You fight, you compete, you annoy each other, you envy each other—but you also protect each other, share jokes, and there’s a lifelong bond underneath the push-and-pull.

programme.title: Silly Things We've All Heard In Our Childhood
programme.desc: Those repetitive warnings, superstitions, myths, and sayings older generations say (“don’t sit like that or you’ll get bald,” etc.). A nostalgic, funny look at how kids heard and internalized them.

programme.title: Struggles Of An Indian Bride
programme.desc: The emotional, logistical, and social pressures a bride faces — from family expectations to dress fittings, guest dramas, and internal doubts. The video underscores how “big day” dreams collide with reality.

programme.title: If Acp Pradyuman (cid) Were Your Boss
programme.desc: The video imagines ACP Pradyuman as a boss in an office setting. It highlights the dramatic style, quirky dialogues, and funny outcomes of his leadership.

programme.title: Neighbourhood Romance: Meeting Your Crush After A Long Time
programme.desc: The story follows two former childhood neighbors who cross paths after a long period of separation. As they reconnect, the video explores the awkward yet charming evolution of their relationship—moving from "childhood crushes" to young adults navigating modern life.

programme.title: Stuff Brothers And Sisters Do
programme.desc: The video is a montage of everyday moments that define the "Tom and Jerry" relationship most siblings share. It captures the transition from intense fighting over trivial things to being each other's biggest support system.

programme.title: Falling For Your Best Friend
programme.desc: The story explores the delicate and often painful realization that you've developed romantic feelings for the one person you can’t afford to lose—your best friend. It follows the emotional journey of two inseparable friends as they navigate the blurry line between platonic comfort and romantic attraction.

programme.title: Signs You Are Becoming Like Your Partner
programme.desc: The video follows a couple as they realize they are slowly losing their individual quirks and merging into a single unit. It captures those "Oh no, I’ve turned into you" moments that every long-term couple eventually faces.

programme.title: When Engineer Falls For Doctor
programme.desc: Two worlds collide: the methodical, formula-loving engineer and the empathetic, patient doctor—catching that awkward transition from friendly banter to “oh, wait I like you” and how they adjust and match.

programme.title: 8 Funny Things That Happen In A Father-Son Relationship
programme.desc: The video is a collection of relatable "micro-moments" that define the bond between a father and son. It captures the transition from a relationship based on authority to one based on friendship, albeit with the classic "dad" quirks remaining intact.

programme.title: Every Roadtrip Ever
programme.desc: The video captures the chaotic, funny, and predictable cycle of an Indian road trip with friends. It moves through the high expectations of the planning phase to the messy (but memorable) reality of actually being on the road.

programme.title: Annoying Things People Do In Your Car
programme.desc: The video is a comedic breakdown of the various ways passengers can drive a car owner (the "driver") absolutely crazy. It captures the struggle of trying to keep your car pristine while your friends treat it like a public lounge.

programme.title: Types Of Shoppers
programme.desc: The video humorously identifies and satirizes the various personas we all adopt the moment we step into a shopping center. It breaks down the stereotypes of shopping and, in classic FilterCopy fashion, flips the script on gendered expectations—showing that men can be just as obsessive or indecisive as women when it comes to fashion.

programme.title: Thoughts You Have While Studying
programme.desc: The video is a comedic dive into the brain of a student who is desperately trying to focus but is constantly derailed by distractions, procrastination, and existential dread. It perfectly captures the "pre-exam" struggle where everything in the world seems more interesting than the textbook in front of you.

programme.title: Backbenchers Vs Toppers
programme.desc: The sketch reimagines the battle between disciplined Toppers and chaotic Backbenchers as a supernatural war. Inspired by Brahmastra, it turns exams and school life into a dramatic, high-stakes fight for ultimate power.

programme.title: Savage Millennial Vs Savage Gen Z
programme.desc: The video explores the generational divide through a series of "savage" exchanges between a Millennial (struggling to keep up) and a Gen Z protagonist (who seems to have a slang for everything). It highlights the hilarious friction that occurs when Millennial "hustle culture" meets Gen Z "boundaries."

programme.title: Life In Boy's School
programme.desc: The video is a high-energy, chaotic exploration of the "survival game" that is an all-boys school. It captures the specific brand of brotherhood, unfiltered humor, and lack of decorum that defines these institutions, moving away from typical co-ed romance to focus purely on the "bro" dynamic.

programme.title: People We See In Every Exam!
programme.desc: The video is a humorous "field guide" to the specific personalities you encounter in a high-pressure examination hall. It captures the frantic, sometimes absurd behavior of students during those three hours of "do or die" academic battle.

programme.title: What If Dhurandhar Was Set In An Office?
programme.desc: The sketch reimagines the intense, high-stakes world of international espionage as the equally "dangerous" jungle of a modern 9-to-5 office. It follows an undercover agent who is sent into a rival firm—not to stop a terror cell, but to prevent the poaching of a major client.

programme.title: Life In A Girls' School
programme.desc: The video explores the "behind-the-scenes" reality of growing up in an all-girls environment—shattering the dainty stereotypes often seen in movies and replacing them with the raw, chaotic, and fiercely loyal brotherhood (or sisterhood) that actually exists.

programme.title: Gen Z Gf Millennial Bf
programme.desc: The story follows a couple navigating the humorous friction that arises when a Millennial's "old school" habits clash with a Gen Z's digital-first lifestyle. It moves beyond simple "slang" jokes to show how their different outlooks on work, romance, and even weekend plans create both conflict and a unique kind of balance.

programme.title: Life In Iit
programme.desc: The video moves past the "glamour" of the IIT brand to show the gritty, exhausting, and heartwarming reality of hostel life. It follows three roommates as they navigate the transition from being "JEE toppers" in their hometowns to being "average students" in a campus full of geniuses.

programme.title: Parents On Facebook
programme.desc: The video is a satirical look at the digital generation gap. It follows a son (Dhruv) as he deals with the social media "awakening" of his mother (Kritika), who approaches Facebook with the same intensity and lack of boundaries she uses in real-life parenting.

programme.title: Confusing Things Girlfriends Say
programme.desc: The video is a comedic "survival guide" for boyfriends trying to navigate the often contradictory and cryptic language of their significant others. It humorously deconstructs the hidden meanings behind common phrases that leave men scratching their heads.

programme.title: Annoying Things Boyfriends Do
programme.desc: While the first video looked at the "mysterious" language of girlfriends, this sketch flips the perspective. It humorously catalogs the predictable, clumsy, and often thoughtless habits of boyfriends that test their partners' patience.

programme.title: What Not To Say In A Relationship
programme.desc: The video follows a series of scenarios where a partner says the absolute worst possible thing at a sensitive moment. It highlights how even a small, unintentionally honest comment can be interpreted as a declaration of war.

programme.title: Things Brothers & Sisters Do
programme.desc: The video is a rapid-fire montage of the daily friction and unspoken affection that defines a sibling bond. It moves past the "emotional" stereotypes to show the hilarious, grounded reality of living under the same roof.

programme.title: Last Diwali Before Moving Out
programme.desc: When you are leaving your house, every moment becomes unforgettable especially festivities like Diwali which makes core memories of growing up Desi.

programme.title: If Google Were A Delhi Boy
programme.desc: The video imagines how Google might behave if it were a stereotypical “Delhi boy” — flashy, informal, always full of attitude. It plays with contrasts like professionalism vs. casual swagger, creating funny scenarios when tech meets typical Delhi-style personality.

programme.title: When You Grow Up With Strict Desi Parents
programme.desc: The video humorously shows the challenges of growing up with strict Desi parents, from high expectations to limited freedom.

programme.title: When You Are The Only Girl In The Group
programme.desc: You’re the lone girl surrounded by guys – every conversation, joke or decision seems to orbit around you. The video captures the awkward, funny, and endearing moments you tweak just to “fit in.”

programme.desc: This crime thriller anthology series, hosted by Ronit Roy, explores the dark side of human nature—where extreme emotions such as greed, jealousy, lust, and obsession spiral into shocking crimes. programme.title: Live Gurbani From Sachkhand Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar
programme.desc: Live Gurbani Kirtan from Gurudwara Sri Sis Ganj Sahib on GTC Punjabi Television brings viewers a sacred spiritual experience directly from one of the most revered historical Gurudwaras of Sikhism, located in the heart of Delhi. This live telecast offers devotees the divine resonance of Gurbani Kirtan, performed by esteemed Ragis, filling homes with peace, devotion, and spiritual reflection. Gurudwara Sri Sis Ganj Sahib stands as a powerful symbol of supreme sacrifice and unwavering faith, marking the martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who laid down his life for the protection of religious freedom and human rights. Through this live broadcast, GTC Punjabi Television connects Sangat across the globe to the serene atmosphere of the Gurudwara, allowing viewers to immerse themselves in Naam Simran, Shabad Kirtan, and the timeless wisdom of Gurbani. The soulful renditions inspire inner calm, strengthen spiritual connection, and spread the universal message of love, equality, and humility as taught by the Sikh Gurus.

Through soulful storytelling, historical references, and meaningful interpretations of Gurbani, this Katha guides the Sangat towards self-reflection, humility, and spiritual awakening. programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

programme.title: Let's Talk Nutrition with Mugdha Pradhan Part 02 | Difference Between Subcutaneous Fat & Visceral Fat
programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.

On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. programme.title: Let's Talk Nutrition with Mugdha Pradhan Part 02 | Difference Between Subcutaneous Fat & Visceral Fat
programme.desc: In this enlightening video, Functional Nutritionist Mugdha Pradhan breaks down the crucial differences between subcutaneous fat and visceral fat, helping you understand their distinct impacts on your health. Subcutaneous fat is the layer found directly under the skin, often noticeable in areas like the abdomen and thighs. While it’s less harmful, managing it is still important for overall fitness. On the other hand, visceral fat lies deeper, wrapping around vital organs and posing significant health risks, including heart disease and diabetes. Mugdha Pradhan offers practical advice on reducing both types of fat through balanced nutrition and lifestyle changes.
